headline: New York sues Polymarket over alleged unlicensed gambling operation
dek: The state wants a court to block the prediction-market company from operating in New York and seeks fines, forfeiture of gains and restitution for users.
body: New York Attorney General Letitia James and Gov. Kathy Hochul filed a lawsuit Thursday accusing Polymarket of operating an unlicensed gambling business through its prediction-market platform.

The attorney general's office said its investigation found that Polymarket lets users wager on sporting events and other uncertain outcomes without a license from the New York State Gaming Commission. The state also alleges the platform is available to users ages 18 to 20, while New York requires people to be at least 21 for mobile sports betting.

The lawsuit asks a state court to stop Polymarket from operating as an unlicensed gambling business. It also seeks the forfeiture of alleged illegal gains, restitution for users who were harmed and fines equal to three times the company's gains, according to the attorney general's announcement.

The Associated Press reported that Polymarket's chief legal officer said the company plans to fight the case. Prediction-market companies argue that users trade contracts with one another rather than place traditional bets, and that the platforms fall under federal Commodity Futures Trading Commission oversight rather than state gambling regulation.

The case is the latest New York challenge aimed at prediction markets. State officials sued Kalshi in July and Coinbase and Gemini in April using similar arguments about unlicensed gambling operations.
author: NorthEast News Desk
